title: Word and body (Dei Verbum 21)
hookLine: the Church venerates scripture as she venerates the Lord's body
tomorrow: can one place be both the mountaintop and the spring?

lines: THE SAME HANDS LIFT THE HOST.
cards: People kiss what they love: a wedding ring, an old photo, the top of a child's head. At Mass, after the Gospel is read, the priest or deacon bends and kisses the page. A few minutes later, the same hands lift the host.
Two gestures of honor, one for a book and one for bread. Dei Verbum 21 sets those two side by side, on purpose.

teach.b: First, the bold sentence. The council says the Church has always venerated the divine scriptures just as she venerates the body of the Lord. That's a strong comparison from a Church that kneels before the Eucharist.
It doesn't say the book is the sacrament. It says the honor runs in the same direction. Second, the table.
Especially in the liturgy, the paragraph says, the Church receives and offers the bread of life from one table, the table of the word of God and of the body of Christ. One table, two courses.
The readings aren't a warm-up before the real thing; they're served from the same place. Third, the meeting.

In the sacred books, Dei Verbum says, the Father in heaven comes lovingly to meet his children and talks with them. That picks up yesterday's friendship: the page is where the conversation keeps happening.
The paragraph calls the word of God support and energy for the Church, food for the soul, a pure and lasting source of spiritual life.
One to tell a friend: as he kisses the book, the Roman Missal has the priest say a short prayer under his breath, that through the Gospel's words our sins be wiped away.

how: At Mass, the priest or deacon who proclaims the Gospel kisses the book afterward, saying a short prayer quietly, and in many churches the Book of the Gospels is carried in procession and placed on the altar.

o: scripture and the Eucharist, honored at one table
a sermon preached while communion is handed out
a promise sealed with a handshake and a kiss

p: word of God and body of Christ
where the Father meets his children

s: at Mass the readings are just the lead-up to communion
the council speaks of one table, of the word of God and the body of Christ.
Dei Verbum 21 says the book of scripture is a sacrament
it says the honor runs the same direction, not that the book is the Eucharist.
the council calls scripture food for the soul
support and energy for the Church, food for the soul, a pure and lasting source.

games.q: at dinner your uncle sets his phone on top of your grandma's old Bible to free a hand, and she quietly moves it. by Dei Verbum 21, what is she doing?
o: honoring the book the way the Lord's body is honored.
protecting an antique from scratches and spills.
following a Church law about phones and holy books.
games.why: Dei Verbum 21: the Church has always venerated the scriptures just as she venerates the body of the Lord.

practice: If there's a Bible nearby, hold it in both hands and feel its weight for a few breaths, then open it anywhere and read one verse slowly. If you pray, you can kiss the page or trace a small cross on it, as is done at Mass.
If no Bible is near, rest your open hands on your knees and let the quiet be the table.

wordCard.voice: Word and body. Dei Verbum 21's pairing: scripture and the Eucharist, served from one table and honored together. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin for table: Dei Verbum 21's one table of God's word and Christ's body.

carryVoice: Your line: word and body. The readings come from the same table as the bread. Until tomorrow.

sources.work: Second Vatican Council, Dogmatic Constitution on Divine Revelation
